specification_basis: Pearson Issue 4 canonical 89 printed reference groups / stable 90 runtime IDs; sample question-level callouts are supporting evidence, not part-level tag unions.
visual_review: Every question crop inspected from SourceRenderer output; original PDF pixels remain authoritative for mathematical typography, diagrams and all joint tariffs.

question_paper.operation: faithful source page extraction; no question rewriting

mark_scheme.operation: faithful source page extraction; no question rewriting

units.difficulty_basis: Apply two polynomial differentiation steps, substitute a supplied stationary abscissa and interpret the second derivative.
units.introduced_year_basis: Polynomial differentiation and stationary-point classification are within AS scope.
units.summary: Differentiate a polynomial and classify its stationary point.

exceptions: Raw (a)(ii) is the single printed joint tariff for a/i/ii; retain all prompts and score its marks once.

units.difficulty_basis: Use arc length to find one radius, infer the second radius from the straight line, and identify the supplementary angle in radians.
units.introduced_year_basis: Radians, arc length and sector area are additional A level content within the broad trigonometry point.
units.summary: Find a sector radius and the area of an adjoining sector.

units.difficulty_basis: Complete both squares, identify the centre and require a strictly positive squared radius.
units.introduced_year_basis: Circle equations, completing the square and the resulting linear inequality are AS content.
units.summary: Complete a circle equation and constrain its constant.

units.difficulty_basis: Separate the constant and reciprocal terms, evaluate at both parameter limits and combine logarithms.
units.introduced_year_basis: Integration of the reciprocal function is additional A level integration content.
units.summary: Evaluate an integral with parameter-dependent limits.

units.difficulty_basis: Rearrange the linear parameter equation and combine the substituted terms over one denominator.
units.introduced_year_basis: Parametric equations are additional A level content.
units.summary: Eliminate a parameter from a rational parametric curve.

units.difficulty_basis: Interpolate using the two supplied model points and explain the physical limitation of continuing a decreasing line.
units.introduced_year_basis: Straight-line modelling and its limitations are within AS scope.
units.summary: Use and critique a linear oil-production model.

units.difficulty_basis: Fit the initial value and a decay factor from a second observation, then evaluate the fitted model.
units.introduced_year_basis: Fitting a basic exponential growth or decay model is within AS scope.
units.summary: Fit and use an exponential oil-production model.

exceptions: Raw (a)(ii) is the single printed joint tariff for a/i/ii; retain all prompts and score its marks once.
Raw (b)(ii) is the single printed joint tariff for b/i/ii; retain all prompts and score its marks once.

units.difficulty_basis: Construct the missing displacement, calculate vector magnitudes and use the cosine rule with the correct triangle angle.
units.introduced_year_basis: Three-dimensional vectors extend the AS two-dimensional vector scope.
units.summary: Find an angle in a triangle defined by three-dimensional vectors.

units.difficulty_basis: Evaluate the function at both supplied endpoints and connect the sign change with continuity.
units.introduced_year_basis: Root-location methods are additional A level numerical content.
units.summary: Locate a root by a sign change.

units.difficulty_basis: Substitute the explicitly supplied function value and derivative into one Newton–Raphson update.
units.introduced_year_basis: Newton–Raphson is additional A level numerical content.
units.summary: Apply a supplied Newton–Raphson step.

units.difficulty_basis: Differentiate the function and use the sign of its derivative throughout the stated domain to rule out another root.
units.introduced_year_basis: Differentiating a logarithm of a linear expression extends AS polynomial and exponential differentiation.
units.summary: Establish uniqueness of a logarithmic-equation root.

exceptions: Use current Issue 4 numerical-method codes: Newton–Raphson 9.3 and trapezium rule 9.4; the older sample exemplification uses earlier numbering.

units.difficulty_basis: Rewrite tangent and cotangent as quotients, use Pythagorean and double-angle identities, then apply a trig-function range restriction.
units.introduced_year_basis: Reciprocal trig functions and double-angle identities are additional A level content.
units.summary: Prove a reciprocal-trig identity and exclude real roots.

units.difficulty_basis: Build the difference quotient, expand a compound angle and justify the limiting terms using the two allowed limits.
units.introduced_year_basis: First principles for trigonometric differentiation extends the AS polynomial first-principles scope.
units.summary: Prove the sine derivative from first principles.

units.difficulty_basis: Set the supplied height model to ground level, solve its quadratic and select the physically valid distance.
units.introduced_year_basis: Solving and interpreting a quadratic model is within AS scope.
units.summary: Find a quadratic model’s physical endpoint.

units.difficulty_basis: Relate the constant term to the height at zero horizontal distance.
units.introduced_year_basis: Interpreting a supplied function model is within AS scope.
units.summary: Interpret a height-model intercept.

units.difficulty_basis: Complete the square and transfer its vertex information to a model with a changed constant term.
units.introduced_year_basis: Completing the square and quadratic maxima are within AS scope.
units.summary: Complete the square and use an adapted quadratic model.

exceptions: Raw (d)(ii) is the single printed joint tariff for d/i/ii; retain all prompts and score its marks once.

units.difficulty_basis: Take logarithms and identify the gradient and intercept of the resulting straight line.
units.introduced_year_basis: Logarithm laws and linearising power models are within AS scope.
units.summary: Linearise a power model using logarithms.

units.difficulty_basis: Read or infer the fitted straight-line parameters and transform back to the original population scale.
units.introduced_year_basis: Estimating parameters with a logarithmic graph is within AS scope.
units.summary: Estimate a population from a logarithmic graph.

units.difficulty_basis: Compare the proposed population with the observed graphical range and explain the unreliability of extrapolation.
units.introduced_year_basis: Interpreting and limiting a logarithmic model is within AS scope.
units.summary: Assess extrapolation from a logarithmic model.

units.difficulty_basis: Use the supplied power model to interpret its coefficient at the natural unit-time input.
units.introduced_year_basis: Interpreting the coefficient of a power model uses AS logarithmic-modelling scope.
units.summary: Interpret a power-model constant.

units.difficulty_basis: Form the ratio of parameter derivatives, evaluate at the supplied parameter value and construct the perpendicular line.
units.introduced_year_basis: Parametric differentiation is additional A level content.
units.summary: Differentiate a parametric curve and establish a normal.

units.difficulty_basis: Use the printed normal equation and a double-angle identity to reduce the intersection to a quadratic and distinguish the second point.
units.introduced_year_basis: Parametric curves and double-angle identities are additional A level content.
units.summary: Find a second intersection of a parametric curve and normal.

units.difficulty_basis: Apply the trapezium rule directly to all supplied equally spaced tabulated values.
units.introduced_year_basis: The trapezium rule is additional A level numerical-integration content.
units.summary: Estimate an area using the trapezium rule.

units.difficulty_basis: Explain how reducing strip width changes the numerical approximation.
units.introduced_year_basis: Accuracy of the trapezium rule is additional A level numerical content.
units.summary: Improve a trapezium-rule estimate.

units.difficulty_basis: Choose integration by parts for a polynomial times a logarithm, apply both limits and simplify the exact logarithmic expression.
units.introduced_year_basis: Integration by parts is additional A level integration content.
units.summary: Evaluate a logarithmic area exactly.

exceptions: Use current Issue 4 numerical-method codes: Newton–Raphson 9.3 and trapezium rule 9.4; the older sample exemplification uses earlier numbering.

units.difficulty_basis: Differentiate the quotient, solve the resulting trig equation over the domain, and distinguish minima after horizontal and vertical transformations.
units.introduced_year_basis: Quotient differentiation with trigonometric functions is additional A level content.
units.summary: Find and transform stationary points of an exponential-trig curve.

exceptions: Raw (b)(ii) is the single printed joint tariff for b/i/ii; retain all prompts and score its marks once.
